title: Engine Oil Change
description: A guided proof-of-concept workflow for performing an engine oil change.
tools: Jack and jack stands or approved lifting equipment
preparation: Confirm the exact vehicle and engine configuration.
Verify the correct oil type, capacity, filter, and service specifications.
Gather required tools, materials, and PPE.
Park on a level surface and secure the vehicle.
Allow the engine to cool to a safe working temperature.

steps.title: Prepare the vehicle
steps.instruction: Secure the vehicle and establish safe access to the oil drain and filter locations.

steps.title: Position the drain pan
steps.instruction: Place the drain pan beneath the engine oil drain location.

steps.title: Drain the engine oil
steps.instruction: Remove the drain plug using the appropriate tool and allow the used oil to drain completely.

steps.title: Replace the oil filter
steps.instruction: Remove the old filter and install the correct replacement according to verified vehicle-specific specifications.

steps.title: Reinstall the drain plug
steps.instruction: Reinstall the drain plug and any required replacement washer using verified vehicle-specific specifications.

steps.title: Add new engine oil
steps.instruction: Add the verified type and quantity of engine oil through the engine oil fill location after verifying the vehicle-specific specification.

steps.title: Verify the service
steps.instruction: Check the oil level and inspect the drain plug and filter areas for leaks.

completionChecks: Drain plug area checked for leaks
Oil filter area checked for leaks
Used oil and filter prepared for proper recycling or disposal

title: Engine Air Filter Replacement
description: A beginner-friendly guide to inspecting and replacing the engine air filter. Follow the vehicle owner's manual for the correct filter and any model-specific instructions.
tools: Screwdriver or socket wrench if required by the air-filter housing
preparation: Confirm the vehicle and engine configuration, and use the owner's manual to identify the correct filter and air-filter housing.
Park on a level surface, switch off the engine, remove the key, and allow the engine bay to cool.
Gather the replacement filter, any required tools, and PPE.
Keep loose clothing, jewelry, and tools clear of moving or hot engine components.

steps.title: Locate the air-filter housing
steps.instruction: Use the owner's manual to find the engine air-filter housing. Do not confuse it with the cabin air-filter compartment.

steps.title: Open the housing
steps.instruction: Release the housing clips or remove its fasteners using the appropriate tool. Lift the cover carefully without pulling or straining attached hoses or wiring.

steps.title: Remove and inspect the old filter
steps.instruction: Note the filter's position and airflow direction, then lift it out. Check the housing and old filter for debris or damage.

steps.title: Clean the housing carefully
steps.instruction: Wipe loose debris from the housing with a clean, lint-free cloth, keeping debris out of the air intake opening. Do not use liquids or blow debris into the intake.

steps.title: Install the replacement filter
steps.instruction: Compare the new filter with the old one to confirm it matches. Seat it in the same orientation, ensuring its edges fit evenly in the housing.

steps.title: Close the housing
steps.instruction: Reinstall the cover and securely fasten all clips or fasteners. Make sure no edges are pinched and any hoses or wiring are back in their original positions.

steps.title: Verify the installation
steps.instruction: Check that the housing is fully closed and the filter is seated. Remove tools and materials from the engine bay before starting the vehicle.

completionChecks: Replacement filter matches the vehicle-specific requirement
Filter is correctly oriented and seated evenly
Air-filter housing is closed and all clips or fasteners are secure
No debris, loose tools, or materials remain in the engine bay
Old filter is disposed of according to local requirements

title: Battery Visual Inspection and Basic Voltage Check
description: A beginner-friendly guide to visually inspecting a vehicle battery and checking its voltage. A voltage reading alone is not a definitive battery-health test; follow vehicle and battery manufacturer guidance.
preparation: Confirm the vehicle's battery location and safety instructions in the owner's manual.
Park safely, switch off the vehicle, remove the key, and work in a well-ventilated area.
Gather the multimeter, flashlight, and PPE.
Keep sparks, flames, jewelry, and tools away from the battery terminals. Do not touch or disconnect the terminals.
Do not continue if the battery is swollen, leaking, cracked, or otherwise damaged; seek professional help.

steps.title: Locate and inspect the battery
steps.instruction: Use the owner's manual to locate the battery. With the vehicle off, look for cracks, swelling, leaks, or visible corrosion without disturbing the terminals.

steps.title: Prepare the multimeter
steps.instruction: Follow the multimeter instructions and set it to measure DC voltage on an appropriate range. If you are unsure of the setting, stop and ask for assistance.

steps.title: Measure the battery voltage
steps.instruction: Following the multimeter and vehicle instructions, place the red probe on the positive terminal and the black probe on the negative terminal. Keep the probes from touching each other or bridging the terminals.

steps.title: Record and interpret the reading
steps.instruction: Record the displayed voltage and compare it with the guidance for the vehicle and battery. A basic voltage reading does not confirm battery health; arrange a professional battery test if the reading is outside guidance or symptoms continue.

steps.title: Finish safely
steps.instruction: Remove the probes carefully without letting them touch each other or bridge the terminals, then put away the meter and tools. Leave the battery and terminals undisturbed.

completionChecks: Battery inspected without touching or disconnecting the terminals
Voltage reading recorded and compared with vehicle or battery guidance
No tools or materials left in the engine bay
Professional battery testing recommended if the reading is outside guidance or symptoms remain
